brief: Polymarket prices Democrat control of the House at 92% and the Senate at 66%, implying a 66% probability of a full Blue Sweep, 27% for a Democrat House and Republican Senate split, and 8% for continued Republican control. The bank cites historical seat losses, PCE inflation rising from 2.3% in April 2025 to 4.1% in May 2026 (3.7% in July), and Trump's approval near 35% as drivers. It expects the economy to stay strong and the Fed to keep raising rates in every scenario, so market impact runs through policy channels rather than growth. A Blue Sweep would impose the strongest constraints on the administration, best protect Fed independence, and is judged best for long Treasuries and, historically, for the S&P 500, averaging +8.8% over three months versus +3.6% for a Republican sweep. A Republican sweep implies the most upward pressure on yields. Separately, the SNB held its rate at 0%, signalled less willingness to intervene in FX markets, and guided to a hike only next year. A Chart of the Week notes US manufacturing PMI hit a 2022 high with the 10-year Treasury yield above 5%.
